claim: The seven SYSTEM CAS command type constants are CAS_GC_RUN, CAS_GC_REBUILD, CAS_DROP_POOL_MEMBER, CAS_FSCK, CAS_FORGET, CAS_GC_STOP, and CAS_GC_START.

getTypeIndexToTypeName derives system-command SQL text from magic_enum::enum_entries by replacing underscores with spaces, so renaming a command enum constant changes its SQL spelling atomically with the parser and formatter.

SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC RUN foo is no longer accepted, while SYSTEM CAS GC RUN foo parses and reaches disk resolution, returning Unknown disk foo for an unknown disk; no backward-compatible alias for the old spelling remains.
The CAS privilege rows exposed by SHOW PRIVILEGES are byte-identical to the rows in 01271_show_privileges.reference:161-167, including tabs.

LIST_OF_CONTENT_ADDRESSED_SETTINGS and CONTENT_ADDRESSED_SETTINGS_SUPPORTED_TYPES remain as internal C++ macros, and the tests/clickhouse-test and tests/config/install.sh occurrences are intentionally deferred to Task 5.
The persisted CasFoldSealFormat fields named gen and the gtest_cas_fold_seal_format.cpp golden value ,"gen":"7" remain unchanged because they are part of the persisted format.
The CasEventType::IndegZero string representation is indegree_zero.

prev_indeg, dropped_by, and cursor are not emitted CasEvent detail keys; the system.cas_log detail-key documentation therefore uses the emitted keys condemn_round, superseded_token, code, and site as examples instead of renaming nonexistent keys.
The spelling indeg_zero in utils/ca-soak/scenarios/BACKLOG.md:273 is retained because it is a dated transcription of a past soak run rather than a live event name.

Snapshot publication records the _snap body with ref_request_controller->putIfAbsentControlled(refSnapshotKey(...)) before calling publishCkptContribution(...); reversing that order makes the ordering test fail.

When checkpoint advancement fails, publishCkpt increments CasRefCkptNotAdvanced, calls advancePublishBackoff, and returns before the snapshot-adoption block; resetPublishBackoff and adoption occur together under one state_mutex hold after a successful CAS.

publishCkpt limits checkpoint CAS attempts with for (attempt < MAX_CKPT_CAS_ATTEMPTS=100) and has no sleep in CasRefCkpt.cpp; each attempt performs one in-memory readCkpt and one casPut, with an additional deadline bound that throws NETWORK_ERROR through throwCasWriteRetryLater if reached.

Every caller of CasRefLedger::acquireReadableRefTableRuntime invokes ensureRefTableRecovered(ns, *rt) before reading state; resolveRef, listRefs, hasAnyRefWithPrefix, and namespaceFilesLifeIfReadable cannot expose an unrecovered cache, and a null runtime returns absence.
The allow_stale parameter of resolveRef is inert (bool /*allow_stale*/), so callers cannot request a stale reference read.

The snapshot-publish test does not detect a no-op resetPublishBackoff; a follow-up should trigger a failure after a successful publish and verify refusal before 1000 ms and admission at 1000 ms to observe reset of the backoff interval.

The snapshot-publish test only brackets the third backoff interval up to 4000 ms and does not pin its lower bound; adding a refusal check after advancing 2000 ms would detect a regression that stops doubling early.

SensitivityCheckOrderingComparisonDiscriminates is not a valid sensitivity check because EXPECT_FALSE(*body_index > *ckpt_index) duplicates the scenario and is weaker than test 1's EXPECT_LT(*body_index, *ckpt_index); the recorded mutation run is the meaningful evidence.

settleSnapshotPublish remains an uncharacterized test subject: its decrement-and-readmit operation must stay under one state_mutex hold so pending_snapshot_publishes cannot transiently reach zero and suppress later chunks of a chunked tenure.

The decommissioner selects owned namespaces exclusively from exact CatalogEntry.ns matches: the victim root itself or victim_srid + "/" as a canonical path-component prefix; it does not derive ownership from NamespaceLifeId, refCkptKey, namespaceStreamPrefix, or an object-storage LIST.

decommissionPoolMember re-reads the catalog for each selected entry and requires exact structural equality with the selected CatalogEntry; a same-name row with a changed incarnation is rejected with CORRUPTED_DATA.

Retirement of a pool-member slot is forbidden while any catalog entry owned by that root remains, including an entry transitioned from Live to Removing during the same decommission call; cleanup proceeds in two phases with GC between the calls.

The decommission retirement tail refuses a stale ownership cut when fresh_retirement_catalog.token != retirement_catalog_cut->token or fresh_retirement_catalog.catalog != retirement_catalog_cut->catalog, reporting catalog changed after the victim ownership check; refusing slot retirement against a stale cut.
A Removing namespace whose exact checkpoint is absent is rejected with CORRUPTED_DATA; the same condition is independently defended by CasRefLedger::dropNamespace through chooseRecoveryGrounding.

When decommission reaches a Removing state before a later namespace fails closed, a SCOPE_EXIT callback preserves the GC liveness signal by invoking request_gc_round; the callback only wakes the serialized GC worker and does not perform catalog work.

The arm-(a) decommission warning reports pool member decommission underway: all N namespace(s) are still owned by this member; upcoming GC rounds perform the final cleanup — re-run this command afterwards to retire the slot, with a count from matching catalog entries; arm (b)'s stale-cut warning remains distinct.

CAS fsck classifies canonical physical keys absent from the catalog at a post-listing observation cut as soft FsckClass::JanitorPending, with report fields namespace_janitor_pending, namespace_janitor_pending_bytes, and namespace_janitor_pending_lives; these fields are excluded from kFsckHardFindings.

CasFsck.cpp uses observe-then-cut classification: it buffers canonical candidates during the physical LIST, reads a fresh catalog cut after listing completes, and classifies candidates against that cut to protect concurrent namespace creation.

Malformed namespace-tree keys remain hard fsck findings, including dirty _files names, zero or uppercase life IDs, and unknown kind directories; canonical dead-life residue is the soft JanitorPending case.

The shared isCleanRelativeNamespaceFileName predicate is used by both Layout::namespaceFileKey and Layout::parseNamespaceFileKey, eliminating the prior parser asymmetry in which the parser accepted nonempty dirty names that the writer rejected.
CommandFsck exposes a janitor-pending detail label and a non-throwing note with the pending count, bytes, and lives; it no longer claims that ca-decommission refuses these keys.

Under the current Stage-A posture, Gc::runNamespaceJanitorPage passes the suppression flag to NamespaceJanitor::runOnePage, which visits unresolved physical life keys but skips every deleteExact when deletes are suppressed; canonical dead-life residue therefore remains pending until destructive rounds are enabled.

Before the fix round, the post-listing post_listing_cut.life_index.resolve(candidate.life_id) call was uncaught, so an ambiguous catalog life ID threw CORRUPTED_DATA and aborted fsck instead of recording a lifeless_keys finding; the corrected code catches CORRUPTED_DATA, records the key, and continues.

The 05020_content_addressed_fsck.reference golden was missing the three columns namespace_janitor_pending, namespace_janitor_pending_bytes, and namespace_janitor_pending_lives, so its 17-field header and row could not match the 20-column SQL output; the golden was regenerated with the columns after lifeless_keys.

CasFsck.AmbiguousLifeUnderAPhysicalKeyIsRecordedNotAborted drives a canonical _files object under life ID 777 into an ambiguity created by catalog rows bad/a and bad/b, ensuring the ambiguity path is exercised by a real physical candidate.

parseNamespaceFileKey now throws on dirty _files keys; NamespaceJanitor::runOnePage catches the exception, records an anomaly, and advances the cursor without clearing page_decided, so malformed keys do not wedge the janitor.
The contentAddressedFsckColumns declaration and appendContentAddressedFsckRow both contain 20 entries, with the three janitor-pending columns immediately after lifeless_keys.

Pool::drainWriterCleanupDuties appends the exact OwnerTransition removal through ref_ledger.appendRefOps, then calls retireBuildSeq(duty->build_seq), then pops the duty; an exception clears draining but retains the duty and does not retire its build sequence.
An uncertain writer duty resolved as reject is drained as a no-op only after the next attempt's resolve-before-reissue GET proves the key absent, and minActive advances past the rejected build.

A rejected precommit body can be nominated and physically swept through real Gc::runRegularRoundReclaiming rounds after successor recovery closes the dead epoch with an arithmetic seal; genuine rejection means ChunkFaultBackend::Mode::Unresolved throws before CountingBackend::putIfAbsent.

The production default UniversePolicy::kDefault is StageA_Suppressed; a suppressed runRegularRound() does not call planManifestCursorPage, emits an orphan_sweep phase with listed == 0, deleted == 0, and suppressed == 1, and leaves the candidate manifest intact.

sweepManifestCursorPage is test-only code: it was moved to src/Disks/tests/cas_sweep_test_support.h as sweepManifestCursorPageForTest, and no production translation unit calls it because exact-token deletion without source-edge retirement or gc/state adoption would recreate the accounting hole.

The Uncertain writer-duty transfer is implemented in PartWriteTxn::~PartWriteTxn, not enqueueWriterCleanupDuty; enqueueWriterCleanupDuty has no Uncertain branch and unconditionally builds and queues the duty.

The real-round orphan accounting test does not detect a broken applied ordinal vector: txns_unapplied == 0 is throw-gated and unmatched_removes == 0 cannot be tripped by the retirement path in its fixture; exposing ledger.applied or retaining the neutrality proof as synthetic is required.

run_cas_gate_per_suite.sh cannot execute parameterized suites whose names contain / because it redirects to a slash-bearing suite-derived log path without creating the nested directory; it also has a fixed 60-second timeout below two passing suites' ASan runtimes.
Q-2 remains open: whether orphan-sweep source edges are retired and durable in the round's gc/state CAS before the TokenMismatch exception is thrown has not been claimed closed.
The CAS system-log members and their default table/config names are cas_gc_log and cas_log; CREATE_PUBLIC_MEMBERS stringifies the member name for both the default table name and the config prefix.
The server setting names are cas_blob_upload_pool_size and cas_condemned_upload_memory_bytes, and the system table is system.cas_mounts.

The canonical metadata storage type is cas: metadataTypeFromString accepts cas, registration uses registerMetadataStorageType("cas", …), and unknown content_addressed fails with UNKNOWN_ELEMENT_IN_CONFIG rather than acting as an alias.

Removing content_addressed_allow_shared_pool and content_addressed_gc_grace_sec from non_cas_keys makes integration configurations that still set either unregistered key fail server startup until Task 6 updates them.

The replication wire-protocol literals are cas_pool_uuid, cas_relink, cas_confirm, cas_source_token, and cas_confirm_answer; both protocol sides are in DataPartsExchange.cpp, so mixed-build clusters fall back to full copies.

src/Disks/tests/gtest_cas_settings.cpp:65 must be updated when Task 5 renames tests/config/config.d/content_addressed_storage_policy_for_merge_tree_by_default.xml, because Task 5's bulk replacements do not cover src/.
The user-visible exception texts containing B16/B34 in DataPartStorageOnDiskBase.cpp and MergeTreeData.cpp predate the naming effort and were intentionally left for a separate cleanup.

In system.cas_gc_log, the user-facing key srid is server_root_id, phase_duration_us is phase_duration_microseconds, and phase-metric keys txns_unapplied and txns_opened are transactions_unapplied and transactions_opened; internal C++/Python identifiers such as String srid, report.srid, and total_us remain unchanged.
clickhouse-disks cas-drop-member prints server_root_id= rather than srid=, and its read-only error uses the same public name; no tree consumer parses the old srid= output key.

The system.cas_mounts columns are started_at and expires_at; the _ms suffix remains on internal MountLease millisecond fields, persisted "sat"/"eat" body keys, cas-inspect JSON keys, holder_expires_at_ms, and log fields because those values are raw epoch milliseconds rather than DateTime64(3) columns.

The 05012_cas_mounts_typed_columns.reference remains unchanged because the query orders expires_at, server_uuid, and started_at in the same alphabetical order as the old names; a missing renamed column would reduce the result from three rows to two and fail the reference.

CAS gtest suite renaming must change only the first argument of TEST, TEST_F, and TEST_P for colliding plain suites; all 62 production-symbol collisions are plain suites, while the two fixture suites do not collide and can be renamed with scoped whole-word edits.
CascadeWriteBuffer is excluded from the CAS* suite set because its Cas prefix is accidental and unrelated to CAS tests.

The CAS suite generator reconciles 296 source Cas suites after excluding CascadeWriteBuffer to 278 runnable suites: 19 compile-guarded suites are excluded and CASBackendContract contributes both CASInMemory/ and CASLocal/ instantiation spellings.

The compile-guarded death-test suites are absent from the release build, 18 are present in ASan, and all 19 are present in a debug build; CASRefInstallSafetyDeathTest is intentionally absent from ASan because MEMORY_TRACKER_DEBUG_CHECKS requires !NDEBUG while sanitizer builds define NDEBUG.

The first CAS suite enumeration missed a multiline INSTANTIATE_TEST_SUITE_P prefix, but the generator caught CasWinnerShape/CASGcCompletedRemovalFenceRace; the invariant must therefore be checked against the built binary rather than only line-based source enumeration.

detail["srid"] in system.cas_log was renamed to server_root_id because it described the same fact already emitted under server_root_id by CasPool and exposed under system.cas_mounts and SYSTEM CAS DROP POOL MEMBER.

runFsckImpl classifies Creating, Live, and Removing catalog entries as protecting a physical candidate when CatalogLifeIndex::resolve returns a value, because the reverse index includes every catalog entry regardless of state.

The orphan-sweep watermark floor is derived from the namespace's own prefix segments and a live mount lease; a namespace rooted outside the pool's server_root_id is permanently ineligible for sweeping regardless of epoch or coverage.
